title: 第十一章促织
lines: 第十一章促织
宋焘抱着天书，在窗前坐了一夜。天亮的时候，他没有合眼，也没有动。他就那样坐着，看月亮落下去，看太阳升起来，看院子里那棵老槐树的影子从西边移到东边。
他想了很久。想周顺，想周顺的娘，想那碗肉汤，想那页血写的字。想自己的娘，想自己为什么没有割肉，没有磕三天三夜的头，没有在书上写“我替我娘死”。他想了很久，想得心口疼。
最后他不想了。他打开天书，翻到新的一页。
这一章，叫《促织》。
宣德年间，宫中盛行斗蟋蟀。上有所好，下必甚焉。每年秋天，朝廷向民间征收蟋蟀，数量之大，前所未有。地方官为了讨好上司，层层加码，把差事压到里正头上。里正又压到百姓头上。谁家交不出蟋蟀，轻则罚款，重则下狱。
华阴县有个里正，叫成名。此人是个读书人，考了多年秀才都没中，最后托关系谋了个里正的差事。他为人老实，不善钻营，做事一板一眼，从不欺压百姓。但正因如此，他在这个位子上坐得很难受。上司嫌他无能，百姓嫌他事多，两头不讨好。
这一年，朝廷征收蟋蟀的文书又下来了。成名的差事，是负责征收本里三十户人家的蟋蟀。他挨家挨户地跑，求爷爷告奶奶，好不容易收上来几只，个头小，品相差，交上去被打回来。上司限期十天，交不够数目，革职查办。
成名急得团团转。他妻子劝他：“你急有什么用？不如出去找找，说不定能逮到好的。”
成名想想也是，便每天早起，提着一个竹篓，到野外去捉蟋蟀。他找遍了附近的田埂、沟渠、草丛，捉到的都是些癞蛤蟆一样的小东西，个头小，没力气，连蹦都蹦不远。他又跑到更远的地方去，翻过一座山，趟过一条河，还是找不到。他累得腿都软了，鞋也磨破了，脚上全是血泡。
眼看期限一天天逼近，成名急得吃不下饭，睡不着觉。他妻子也跟着着急，两个人相对无言，坐在屋里唉声叹气。
这天夜里，成名做了一个梦。梦里，他站在一座祠堂前，门开着，里面供着一尊神像，看不清是谁。神像前跪着一个小孩，八九岁的样子，穿着红肚兜，扎着两个小辫子，正在磕头。小孩磕完头，站起来，转过身，冲他笑了笑。
“成伯伯，你是在找蟋蟀吗？”
成名点点头。小孩说：“你跟我来。”
小孩走出祠堂，往东边走。成名跟在后面，走了一段路，到了一片荒草地。小孩蹲下来，扒开草丛，指着地上一只蟋蟀说：“你看。”
成名低头一看，那只蟋蟀个头不大，但通体乌黑，油光发亮，两只触须又长又挺，像两根钢针。它蹲在草叶上，一动不动，威风凛凛，像一员大将。
成名又惊又喜，伸手去捉。蟋蟀一跳，跳到了小孩的手心里。小孩捧着蟋蟀，递给成名。
“成伯伯，给你。”
成名接过蟋蟀，千恩万谢。他问小孩叫什么名字，小孩笑了笑，没说话，转身走了。成名追上去，想问个清楚，脚下一绊，摔了一跤，醒了。
他睁开眼，天已经亮了。他躺在床上，出了一身冷汗。他妻子问他怎么了，他把梦说了一遍。妻子说：“做梦的事，哪能当真？”
成名不信。他爬起来，穿上鞋，往东边走。走了大约一里路，果然看见一片荒草地。他蹲下来，扒开草丛——一只蟋蟀趴在草叶上，通体乌黑，油光发亮，和他梦见的那个一模一样。
他的手在发抖。他慢慢地伸出手，轻轻地罩住蟋蟀，捧在手心里。蟋蟀没有挣扎，安安静静地趴在他掌心，像等着他来。
成名捧着蟋蟀，一路跑回家。他把蟋蟀放进一只瓦盆里，喂它吃栗子，喂它喝水，把它养得好好的。这只蟋蟀个头虽不大，但性情凶猛，放进什么蟋蟀都被它咬得落花流水。
成名大喜过望，准备明天一早就把蟋蟀交上去。
成名有个儿子，叫成安，九岁。这孩子聪明伶俐，调皮捣蛋，没少让成名操心。这天，成安放学回家，看见父亲屋里多了一只瓦盆，好奇地凑过去看。他掀开盖子，看见里面有一只蟋蟀，乌黑发亮，威风凛凛。
他忍不住伸手去摸。蟋蟀受惊，猛地一跳，从盆里跳出来，跳到地上，蹦了几下，跳出了门外。成安慌了，追出去找。蟋蟀在院子里蹦来蹦去，他扑了几次都没扑到。最后一次，他猛地扑过去，手按住了蟋蟀，但力道太大，把蟋蟀按死了。
成安看着手心里那团黑乎乎的尸体，吓得浑身发抖。他知道，这是父亲的命根子。父亲找了好几个月才找到这一只，全家人的指望都在它身上。现在它死了，什么都完了。
他怕父亲打他，更怕父亲交不上蟋蟀被革职查办。他越想越怕，怕得浑身发抖，牙齿咯咯响。最后他做了一个决定。
他跑出家门，跑到村东头的那口井边，闭上眼睛，跳了下去。
成名回到家，看见瓦盆空了，蟋蟀不见了。他问妻子，妻子说不知道。他又问儿子，找不到儿子。他慌了，满村去找。

Chapter 11 Promoting Weaving
Song Tao held the Book of Heaven in his arms and sat in front of the window all night. At dawn, he didn't close his eyes or move. He just sat like that, watching the moon set, watching the sun rise, and watching the shadow of the old locust tree in the yard move from the west to the east.
He thought about it for a long time. I miss Zhou Shun, I miss Zhou Shun's mother, I miss that bowl of broth, I miss that page of words written in blood. I miss my mother, and wonder why I didn’t cut off my flesh, kowtow for three days and nights, or write “I died for my mother” in the book. He thought about it for a long time, and his heart ached.
Finally he didn't want to. He opened the book and turned to a new page.
This chapter is called "Promoting Weaving".
During the Xuande period, cricket fighting was popular in the palace. What is good at the top will be bad at the bottom. Every autumn, the imperial court collected crickets from the people. The number was unprecedentedly large. In order to please his superiors, the local officials increased the pressure at every level and put the errands on Li Zheng. Li Zheng is on top of the people again. Anyone who fails to hand over the crickets will be fined at least, or jailed at worst.
There is a right thing in Huayin County called becoming famous. This person is a scholar. He failed to pass the scholar examination for many years, and finally found a decent job through connections. He is an honest man, not good at trying to get things done, he is strict in doing things, and he never bullies the people. But because of this, he felt uncomfortable sitting in this seat. His superiors thought he was incompetent, and his people thought he had too many things to do. Both sides were unhappy.
This year, the imperial court's documents for the collection of crickets came down again. His famous job was to collect crickets from thirty households in this area. He ran from house to house, begging his grandfather to tell his grandma, and finally collected a few of them. They were small in size and of poor quality, but they were beaten back after being handed over. The boss has a ten-day deadline and if the amount is not enough, he will be dismissed and investigated.
The rush to fame is overwhelming. His wife advised him: "What's the point of being anxious? It's better to go out and look for him. Maybe you can catch something good."
Thinking about becoming famous, he got up early every day, carried a bamboo basket, and went to the wild to catch crickets. He searched the nearby fields, ditches, and grass, and all he caught were small toad-like things. They were small, weak, and couldn't even jump far. He ran further away, climbed a mountain, and waded across a river, but still couldn't find it. His legs were so tired that they were weak, his shoes were worn out, and his feet were covered in blood blisters.
Seeing the deadline approaching day by day, I was so anxious about becoming famous that I couldn't eat or sleep. His wife was also anxious, and the two of them sat in silence in the room and sighed.
That night, Cheng Ming had a dream. In the dream, he was standing in front of an ancestral hall. The door was open and there was a statue of a god inside. He could not see who it was. Kneeling in front of the statue is a child, about eight or nine years old, wearing a red bellyband and two pigtails, kowtowing. After the child kowtowed, he stood up, turned around, and smiled at him.
"Uncle Cheng, are you looking for crickets?"
Fame nodded. The child said: "Follow me."
The child walked out of the ancestral hall and walked east. Cheng Ming followed behind and walked for a while until they reached a deserted grassland. The child squatted down, pushed aside the grass, pointed at a cricket on the ground and said, "Look."
Cheng Ming looked down and saw that the cricket was not big, but its body was black and shiny, and its two tentacles were long and straight, like two steel needles. It squatted on the grass blades, motionless, majestic, like a general.
I was surprised and happy to become famous, so I reached out to catch it. The cricket jumped into the child's hand. The child held a cricket and handed it to Fengming.
"Uncle Cheng, here you go."
Become famous and take over the crickets, thank you a thousand times. He asked the child what his name was. The child smiled, said nothing, turned and left. Cheng Ming chased after him and wanted to ask clearly, but he tripped and fell and woke up.
He opened his eyes and it was already dawn. He lay on the bed and broke out in a cold sweat. His wife asked him what was wrong and he told him his dream. The wife said: "How can a dream be taken seriously?"
Do not believe in fame. He got up, put on his shoes, and walked east. After walking about a mile, I saw a piece of grassland. He squatted down and opened the grass - a cricket lay on the grass blades, black and shiny, exactly like the one in his dream.
His hands were shaking. He slowly stretched out his hand, gently covered the cricket, and held it in his hand. The cricket didn't struggle and lay quietly in his palm, as if waiting for him to come.
Famous held the cricket in his hands and ran all the way home. He put the cricket into an earthen basin, fed it chestnuts and water, and raised it well. Although this cricket is not big, it has a ferocious temperament. It will bite any cricket you put in it.
I am overjoyed to be famous and am ready to hand in the cricket early tomorrow morning.
Chengming has a son named Chengan, who is nine years old. This child is smart and naughty, and has a lot to worry about when he becomes famous. On this day, Cheng An came home from school and saw an extra clay basin in his father's house. He curiously went over to take a look. He opened the lid and saw a cricket inside, shiny black and majestic.
He couldn't help but reach out and touch it. The cricket was frightened, jumped out of the basin, jumped to the ground, jumped a few times, and jumped out of the door. Cheng'an panicked and chased him out to find him. Crickets were jumping around in the yard, but he pounced several times but failed to catch them. For the last time, he rushed forward and held down the cricket with his hand, but the force was too strong and killed the cricket.
Cheng An looked at the black body in his hand and trembled with fear. He knew that this was his father's lifeblood. My father searched for several months before he found this one, and the whole family was counting on it. Now that it is dead, everything is lost.
He was afraid that his father would beat him, and he was even more afraid that his father would be dismissed and investigated if he failed to hand over the crickets. The more he thought about it, the more frightened he became. His whole body was shaking with fear and his teeth were chattering. Finally he made a decision.
He ran out of the house, ran to the well at the east end of the village, closed his eyes, and jumped in.
After becoming famous, I returned home and saw that the pot was empty and the crickets were gone. He asked his wife and she said she didn't know. He asked his son again, but he couldn't find him. He panicked and searched all over the village.
